title: Prove safe one-disk NixOS production cutover
goal: Prove a reversible one-disk production cutover for the sole Heim-PC SN850X without performing the production cutover: rehearse the exact canonical LUKS2+Btrfs topology from a blank virtual disk, classify all migration-relevant data, establish independently restorable off-host backup capacity and offline recovery material, and produce an exact reviewed destructive plan whose execution remains separately authorized.

approval.note: This task may prepare tests, backup/recovery evidence and a destructive plan, but it does not authorize partitioning, mkfs, LUKS/EFI mutation, firmware changes, reboot or NixOS switch on the production host.

acceptance.assertion: Starting from a blank disposable virtual disk, the exact canonical target topology GPT + EFI + recovery surface + LUKS2 + Btrfs with @root, @nix, @persist, @home, @data and @containers is created declaratively, unlocked, mounted, booted and read back successfully; the earlier LUKS+ext4 VM proof is not substituted for this topology.
Fresh inventory classifies migration-relevant non-reproducible data separately from caches/rebuildable state; current scoped Restic success is not treated as proof of complete cutover coverage.

Every critical migration data class has sufficient independent off-host storage and a staged restore test proving representative usable content; the presently capacity-constrained backup target must be remediated or replaced before this gate can pass.

Independent bootable recovery media plus the required offline host/control closure, source/lock/trust roots and LUKS/recovery material are verified without Grabowski, Bureau, network or the production system SSD.

A fresh device-bound plan identifies the exact production disk, partition/ESP/LUKS/Btrfs effects, point of no return, rollback/reconstruction path, expected approved system closure and mandatory post-boot readback; no device enumeration assumption is used as identity.

This task terminates before any production partitioning, formatting, LUKS mutation, EFI/Secure-Boot key mutation, firmware write, reboot into a new production OS or NixOS switch; such effects require a later explicit destructive-action approval bound to fresh recovery evidence.

All VM/recovery/plan validation and required repository CI are green and the final one-disk plan receives explicit independent review before the task is considered ready for a separate cutover decision.
